text:
anna: Hey, running into a weird one in the Kotlin SDK sample app when uploading large files via Retrofit + OkHttp on Android 12/13 emulators. Uploads intermittently fail with 503 and sometimes the server reports truncated bodies.

raj: Ugh. Is this the chunked streaming upload path (RequestBody streaming) or buffering into memory first?

anna: Streaming. We implemented a `RequestBody` that writes bytes from a FileInputStream and reports progress. Works fine on device, flaky on emulator.

max: Emulator often has networking quirks. Any stack traces or server logs? 503 usually from a proxy/fronting LB.

anna: Server logs show connection reset during HTTP/1.1 chunked body -> LB returns 503. No obvious exception client-side besides `java.io.IOException: unexpected end of stream`.

katie: Could be OkHttp's connection reuse + coroutine cancellation racing with the stream. Are you using `enqueue` + coroutines integration or `suspend` adapter?

anna: We're using a custom suspend CallAdapter that runs `call.execute()` inside `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`. We also have `retryOnConnectionFailure(true)` enabled.

raj: That combination can cause partial writes to be retried, which without a repeatable body will corrupt the protocol. OkHttp will only retry idempotent requests when it can safely resend; streaming bodies aren't repeatable.

max: Also check `OkHttpClient.dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost` and `connectionPool` settings — the emulator's NAT and flakey sockets make timeouts cascade into connection starvation. We saw similar with streaming downloads.

anna: Repro steps I used: 1) Start local test LB (nginx) that proxies to a simple upload backend; 2) Run emulator Android 13; 3) Trigger 15 parallel uploads of a 30MB file. After ~10-30s a subset fail with `unexpected end of stream` and the backend shows partial chunked body.

katie: Can you paste the client config?

anna: Sure:

```
val ok = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .readTimeout(120, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .writeTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64; maxRequestsPerHost = 16 })
  .build()
```

raj: A few suggestions: 1) turn off `retryOnConnectionFailure` for streaming endpoints; 2) increase `maxRequestsPerHost` temporarily to avoid queueing; 3) make the body repeatable (buffer a limited-size window) if you must allow retries; 4) add a `Retry-After` style backoff at the app layer.

max: Also try setting `writeTimeout` to a finite value (like 5m) instead of 0 — 0 disables and can hide underlying socket stalls. And consider `okhttp` `ConnectionSpec` changes for older TLS on emulator.

anna: Quick test: turned off retries and set `maxRequestsPerHost=32` — failures dropped significantly in the emulator repro. Will run more.

katie: For SDK parity, we should document that the Kotlin suspend adapter must not rely on OkHttp automatic retries for non-repeatable bodies. That bites teams that assume parity with Java blocking `execute()` semantics.

raj: Agreed. We should add a note in devex docs and an example interceptor to guard streaming uploads:

```
class NoRetryForStreamingInterceptor: Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val req = chain.request()
    if (!requestHasRepeatableBody(req)) {
      // disable retry by adding header consumed by networking layer
      val newReq = req.newBuilder().header("x-sdk-no-retry", "1").build()
      return chain.proceed(newReq)
    }
    return chain.proceed(req)
  }
}
```

max: We can also add a small test app in samples/ showing a safe pattern: either buffer up to N MB (configurable) or use multipart uploads with resumable checkpoints.

anna: I'll open a PR to add docs + sample change. Also adding an emulator-only checklist: increase per-host requests, finite write timeout, and disable automatic retry for streaming endpoints.

ci-bot: PR opened: #4523 — devex/doc: kotlin-sdk streaming upload guidance + sample app.

katie: Awesome. Can you include a short snippet showing how to implement a repeatable `RequestBody` wrapper for small files? That will help onboarding. :+1:

anna: Will do. Thanks for the pointers — much less noisy now when I repro with the changes.

raj: Nice. If you still see truncated bodies after this, ping me and I'll help dig into emulator NAT / tcpdump traces.

anna: Will do. Thanks everyone.
